$comment: Authored port of the hand-written registry group eventbridge-events (docs/plans/compat-coverage-modelgen.md §3.11, G6, #1116). One spec in place of the five per-language implementations that exist and the two (dotnet-sdk, rust-sdk) that never did — 2 tests of parity debt per missing suite. It runs today under the shadow name eventbridge-events-shadow, beside the natives, so the nightly can compare the two per (suite, test); the flip PR renames this group to eventbridge-events, adds the scenario field to the hand-written registry.json entry, and deletes the native code. The clauses are the union of what the five natives assert — see compat/model/README.md § Authored scenarios. This group is PutEvents' own answer only: no native here verifies that an event reached a target, which is eventbridge-target-fanout's job and the cross-service gap #1931.

groups.$comment: Every event goes to one custom bus created in setup and deleted in teardown (#388: each EventBridge group uses its own bus). go-sdk, cli, python-sdk and java-sdk all create a bus in setup, but they do not all use it: node-js-sdk puts both tests' events on the default bus, go-sdk puts PutEventsBatch's there, and java-sdk puts PutEvents' there — the default bus is shared by every concurrent run and every other group, which a per-run bus is the whole point of avoiding. cli and python-sdk put both tests on their own bus, and that is the shape taken. No clause is wrapped in `eventually`: PutEvents answers synchronously with one result entry per request entry, and every native reads that answer directly.
groups.name: eventbridge-events-shadow

tests.$comment: All five natives assert FailedEntryCount is 0 — go-sdk, cli and python-sdk as `> 0` fails, node-js-sdk as `<= 0`, java-sdk as equality — which is one claim, spelled here as equality. Entries[0].EventId is the union's addition: AWS documents PutEventsResultEntry.EventId as the ID of a successfully ingested event and ErrorCode/ErrorMessage as present only on a failed one, so a zero failure count and an accepted entry with an id are the same statement read from both ends; Entries[1] missing pins that one request entry got one result entry, the single-entry half of cli's count check below. The Source/DetailType/Detail literals differ in every native (my.app/order, oc.cli/TestEvent, compat.test/CompatTest, com.example.overcast/TestEvent, compat.<runId>/CompatTest) and nothing reads them back; a fixed source naming this group is used, since the bus is already per run.
tests.name: PutEvents

tests.$comment: go-sdk, python-sdk and node-js-sdk send five entries, cli two, java-sdk one (its PutEventsBatch is a single event on the custom bus, implemented as putEventsCustomBus). Five is the majority and the only size that is a batch in every sense. All five natives assert FailedEntryCount is 0; cli alone also asserts the response carries exactly as many result entries as it sent, which is expressed here as Entries[4] present and Entries[5] missing — `equals` on a list's length has no spelling in the IR, and the index pair is the same claim exactly. Every result entry carrying an EventId is the union's addition, on the same AWS-documented grounds as PutEvents'. Detail carries each entry's index, as go-sdk, python-sdk and node-js-sdk do; the IR has no loop, so the five entries are written out.
tests.name: PutEventsBatch
